svg.aria-label: Sequence of an SMC call. Case A, on every boot: the Linux kernel puts PSCI CPU_ON in x0 and executes smc; the CPU traps to BL31 at EL3, which powers up the next core and returns success with eret. Case B, only with OP-TEE: an application's ioctl reaches the kernel's OP-TEE driver, which executes smc; BL31 saves the normal-world context and enters OP-TEE at S-EL1, the trusted application uses a key in secure memory, and the result returns through BL31 to the kernel and the application.
svg.text: smc is a deliberate trap into EL3. BL31 reads the function ID in x0 and either answers itself (PSCI, SiP) or forwards to OP-TEE.
A · EVERY BOOT OF THIS BOARD: Linux starts CPUs 1-3 through PSCI
powers up core 1 via the GPC
B · ONLY WITH OP-TEE BUILT IN: an app uses a key it never sees
uses the key in secure-only RAM
eret · back down to the caller's level
